topic: Lady Be Good (B-24D 41-24301): the bomber found in the Libyan Desert, told from the record
research_summary: Proven topic: top video 3.2M views (Scary Interesting, 17 min), several 400K+ long-forms. Most titles say 'vanished without a trace' or 'flew itself home'. Underserved angle: a documented, source-on-screen telling that shows where the records disagree (discovery month, whether the plane joined the formation, walk distance, water carried) and uses the diary only as quoted by published sources.

data_points.claim: Lady Be Good's first combat mission was the 4 April 1943 Naples raid; it never returned
The wreck was spotted in 1958 roughly 440 miles southeast of Benghazi
Diary found in Toner's pocket in February 1960; last entry dated Monday 12 April
Five crew remains found 11 Feb 1960; Shelley and Ripslinger found later in 1960; Moore never found
Wreck moved to Tobruk in August 1994; parts displayed at the National Museum of the USAF
